source: We need to <define> raise </define> the motivation level in the company .
reference: (transitive) To create, increase or develop.
hypothesis: (transitive) To increase the level of.
manual_notes: “Increase the level of” is narrower than “create, increase or develop,” but overlaps with the increase sense. Majority label is reliable; two annotators marked hallucination, so this is borderline.

source: That new project manager is just the one to <define> ramrod </define> this through to completion .
reference: (transitive) To force.
hypothesis: (transitive, idiomatic) To push (something) through with great effort.
manual_notes: “Force” and “push something through with great effort” overlap in some contexts but are not equivalent in all contexts. Four of five annotators marked reliable.

source: Democritus , as he is described by Hippocrates and Laertius , was a little <define> wearish </define> old man , very melancholy by nature , averse from company in his latter days , and much given to solitariness   [ … ] .
reference: (obsolete, or, dialectal) Sickly, wizened, feeble.
hypothesis: Resembling or characteristic of a worn-out person.
manual_notes: Both descriptions suggest weakness or being worn-out, but the hypothesis paraphrases the idea rather than preserving the exact definition. All five annotators marked reliable; likely a model false positive.

source: Tiers of grandstands with comfortable plush - covered <define> armchaired </define> seats will surround the “ Dress Circle , ” whilst the “ mournful silence of the fells ” will be drowned by the droning of the day - trip aeroplanes encircling our summits , from Blackpool and the Isle of Man .
reference: Furnished with armchairs.
hypothesis: Having an armchair.
manual_error_category: Semantic mismatch / number or possession detail
manual_notes: “Furnished with armchairs” means equipped with armchairs; “having an armchair” can imply one armchair rather than a furnished space. Gold is split 3–2, so boundary ambiguity is plausible.

source: A whole <define> pathful </define> of fallen flowers go off down to the waters , this is the morning young Ruan Zhao reaches Mount Tian - tai .
reference: Enough to fill a path.
hypothesis: A large amount of something.
manual_notes: “Enough to fill a path” describes quantity sufficient to fill a path, while “a large amount of something” is broader and loses the path-related constraint. Three of five annotators marked hallucination.

source: He might ignore it for three months and then , one midnight , drink <define> sippingly </define> and methodically from a water glass , lying back on the cot an hour later with the world all closed down , nothing left of it but a terminal throbbing ache in his forebrain .
reference: With sips.
hypothesis: In a sipping manner.
manual_notes: “With sips” and “in a sipping manner” are closely related adverbial meanings. Four annotators marked hallucination, but the semantic difference appears subtle.

source: Я бы непрочь еще чашечку чая.
reference: I would like to have some more tea.
hypothesis: I wouldn't miss another cup of tea.
manual_notes: “I would like to have some more tea” expresses desire for more tea; “I wouldn't miss another cup of tea” has a different polarity/idiomatic meaning. Annotators split 3–2, but the semantic change is substantial.

source: Ты знаешь, что он сделал?
reference: Do you know what he has done?
hypothesis: You know what he did?
manual_error_category: Valid paraphrase missed by gold/model boundary
manual_notes: “Do you know what he has done?” and “You know what he did?” are close paraphrases with a small question-form difference. All annotators marked reliable, suggesting a model false positive.

source: Ты мог бы сказать правду.
reference: You could've told the truth.
hypothesis: You could tell the truth.
manual_notes: “Could've told” refers to a past opportunity or criticism; “could tell” can refer to present/future ability. The tense/aspect shift may change meaning. Annotators split 3–2.

source: Я силён в японском языке.
reference: I'm good at Japanese.
hypothesis: I am strong in Japanese.
manual_notes: “Good at Japanese” and “strong in Japanese” are idiomatically close, though the latter can be less natural. Three annotators marked hallucination and two reliable; likely a borderline translation.

source: Том промыл за ушами.
reference: Tom washed behind his ears.
hypothesis: Tom washed his ears.
manual_notes: The hypothesis says Tom washed his ears but omits “behind,” which specifies the location. This is a small but potentially meaningful detail loss; annotators split 3–2.

source: Как поживаете?
reference: How's life?
hypothesis: How do you live?
manual_notes: “How's life?” is a greeting asking about someone's general well-being; “How do you live?” asks about manner of living. The hypothesis changes the intended question.

source: Sometimes it's enough.
reference: Sometimes it's enough.
hypothesis: Sometimes, it's enough for me.
manual_notes: The hypothesis adds “for me,” introducing a personal qualifier absent from the reference. The addition may be harmless in context but is not entailed by the reference; annotators split 3–2.

source: Can I just say one thing?
reference: Can I just say one thing?
hypothesis: CAN I JUST SAY ONE THINGS?
manual_notes: The hypothesis changes “one thing” to “one things,” creating a number/agreement error while retaining the intended meaning. Annotators split 3–2; this may reflect a strict form-sensitive label.

source: You've got to be kidding me.
reference: You've got to be kidding me.
hypothesis: You've got to be kidding me, by the way.
manual_notes: The hypothesis adds “by the way,” a discourse marker absent from the reference. The core phrase is preserved; four annotators marked reliable, so this is a likely false positive on a minor addition.

source: It has a ring to it.
reference: It has a ring to it.
hypothesis: It makes a sound.
manual_notes: “It has a ring to it” usually means something sounds appealing or memorable; “It makes a sound” is literal and changes the idiomatic meaning.

source: Hold it right there.
reference: Hold it right there.
hypothesis: Standby.
manual_notes: “Hold it right there” is a command to stop; “Standby” means wait or be ready and is not necessarily equivalent. The model may have accepted broad command similarity.

source: I became sick with worry.
reference: I became sick with worry.
hypothesis: I became troubled.
manual_notes: “Became sick with worry” expresses strong anxiety; “became troubled” is more general and weaker, omitting the intensity and physical/idiomatic force.

source: The forcible administration of poison is by no means a new thing in criminal annals .
reference: Done by force , forced .
hypothesis: Having the power to force .
manual_notes: “Done by force, forced” describes an action or state caused by force; “having the power to force” describes ability. The hypothesis shifts from occurrence/result to capability. All annotators marked reliable, so inspect benchmark context before treating this as a clear semantic error.

source: The chieftain was well versed in Creek history .
reference: Of or pertaining to the Creek tribe .
hypothesis: A member of a tribe inhabiting the Indian plains of the United States of America
manual_notes: The reference describes something pertaining to the Creek tribe; the hypothesis defines a member of a tribe on the American plains. Related words do not preserve the same relation or definition. Annotators split 3–2.

source: The sewing machine is in disrepair .
reference: The state of being in poor condition , in need of repair .
hypothesis: The state of being in poor condition ; deterioration , disuse ,
manual_notes: The reference says poor condition requiring repair; the hypothesis adds “deterioration, disuse,” which are related but not identical concepts. Four annotators marked reliable, indicating a possible overly strict or context-sensitive boundary.

source: A contact device installed at an outlet for the connection of an attachment plug is a receptacle . A multiple receptacle is a single device consisting of two or more receptacles .
reference: A contact device installed at an outlet for the connection of an attachment plug ( typically by receiving the plug 's prongs ) to supply portable appliances or equipment .
hypothesis: A device that connects .
manual_notes: The reference specifies an outlet contact device for connecting a plug and supplying equipment; “a device that connects” omits the defining function and is too broad.

source: bonded duties
reference: Secured by bond .
hypothesis: Having a bond .
manual_notes: “Secured by bond” indicates being guaranteed or bound through a bond; “having a bond” is broader and does not necessarily imply secured/guaranteed status. Three of five annotators marked hallucination.

source: and , lo ! a palace towering seems , / With Parian pillars and metallic beams .
reference: Made of or containing metal .
hypothesis: Of or pertaining to metal .
manual_notes: “Made of or containing metal” describes material composition; “of or pertaining to metal” describes association with metal. These senses overlap but are not identical. Annotators split 3–2.

source: Kodayake yawancin dabbobi da ke wurin killace dabbobin sun saba da ganin mutane, duk da haka namomin daji na da hadari don haka kada a basu abinci ko a tsokane su.
reference: Though many of the animals in the park are used to seeing humans, the wildlife is nonetheless wild and should not be fed or disturbed.
hypothesis: Although most animals in the grazing area are familiar with humans, wildlife are dangerous and therefore not to be fed or harmed.
manual_notes: The hypothesis changes “used to seeing humans” to “familiar with humans,” then adds that wildlife are dangerous and changes “disturbed” to “harmed.” These alter the source meaning. Annotators split 3–2.

source: ཁོ་གིས་ ནད་རླུང་མར་ཕབ་ ག་དེ་ཅིག་འབད་ནི་ཨིན་ན་ གྱངས་ཁ་མ་སླབ་རུང་ རྒྱ་ནག་གི་དཔལ་འབྱོར་ལུ་གཞི་བཞག་སྟེ་འབད་འོང་ཟེར་བཤད་ཅི།
reference: He did not set a figure for the cuts, saying they will be made based on China's economic output.
hypothesis: He did not specify the extent of the emissions reduction, but said it would be based on China's economy.
manual_notes: “Figure for the cuts” becomes “extent of the emissions reduction,” and “China's economic output” becomes “China's economy.” This may preserve the broad meaning while losing specificity. All five gold labels are not shown as unanimous; the annotator split is 3–2.

source: O le piramita tele na faia e faʻamanatu ai Farao Khufu, ma o le tele o tama’i piramita, o tuugamau, ma malumalu na fausia e fa’amamaluina ai faletua o Khufu ma tagata uma o le aiga.
reference: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
hypothesis: The great pyramids were built in honour of Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor the wife of Khufu and all his family.
manual_notes: “Wives and family members” becomes “the wife of Khufu and all his family,” changing plural wives to singular wife and slightly changing the family-member wording. Four annotators marked reliable, so the error may be borderline.

source: प्राकृतिक वातावरण मे पौधा सभ सँ नीक लगैत अछि, एहि कारण "सिर्फ एक" नमूना हटेबाक प्रलोभनक विरोध करू।
reference: Plants look their best when in a natural environment, so resist the temptation to remove even "just one" specimen.
hypothesis: Plants are best suited to natural environments, so we resist the temptation to take "only one" sample.
manual_notes: The hypothesis changes the general instruction “resist the temptation” to “we resist” and “specimen” to “sample.” It changes imperative/general advice into a first-person statement. Four annotators marked hallucination.

source: Long 1989 em i helpim long kamapim The Simpsons wantaim Brooks na Groening, na em i bin mekim wok bilong kisim namba wan tim bilong raitim stori bilong dispela 'show'.
reference: In 1989 he helped create The Simpsons with Brooks and Groening, and was responsible for hiring the show's first writing team.
hypothesis: Throughout 1989, I helped create The Simpsons with Brooks and Groening, and I was involved in getting the first team to write a story for the show.
manual_error_category: Pronoun / role and event detail shift
manual_notes: The reference uses third person (“he”) and says the person was responsible for hiring the first writing team; the hypothesis changes to first person and weakens hiring to being involved in getting a team to write a story.

source: ၵူၺ်းၵေႃႈ လွင်ႈမူၼ်ႉမႄး ဢမ်ႇၼၼ် လွင်ႈတုၵ်းယွၼ်း သင်ၵေႃႈလီ ဢွၼ်တၢင်းသုတ်း ထုၵ်ႇလီသူင်ႇၸူးတီႈ ၶွမ်ႇပၼီႇတၢင်တူဝ်ၵၢၼ်ဢွၵ်ႇၶၢဝ်းတၢင်းၼၼ်ႉယူႇယဝ်ႉ ဢမ်ႇထုၵ်ႇလီသူင်ႇထိုင်တီႈ ႁူင်းလိုဝ်ႈသဝ်းၼၼ်ႉ ၵမ်းသိုဝ်ႈ။
reference: Any amendments or requests though should be coursed through the travel agent first and not directly with the hotel.
hypothesis: However, any amendment or appeal should first be sent to the travel agent and not to the hotel immediately.
manual_notes: “Request” becomes “appeal,” and “not directly with the hotel” becomes “not to the hotel immediately.” The broad advice is similar, but directness and timing are not exactly the same. Annotators split 3–2.

source: Yes, but a political solution is not an end in itself.
reference: Yes, but a political solution is not an end in itself.
hypothesis: A political solution isn't the only one.
manual_notes: “A political solution is not an end in itself” means it is not sufficient as the ultimate goal; “isn't the only one” means other solutions exist. These propositions are not equivalent. Annotators split 3–2.

source: Europe may indeed suffer from high unemployment, but it has never been as wealthy.
reference: Europe may indeed suffer from high unemployment, but it has never been as wealthy.
hypothesis: Europe has never been as rich as it is now.
manual_notes: The reference says Europe has never been as wealthy (in context, likely a comparison over time); the hypothesis says Europe has never been as rich as it is now, which is close in wording but can change the comparison structure. Four annotators marked reliable, so this is likely a model false positive.

source: We have adopted seven amendments in the Economic Affairs Committee, Commissioner.
reference: We have adopted seven amendments in the Economic Affairs Committee, Commissioner.
hypothesis: The economic affairs committee has seven amendments.
manual_notes: The reference says the speaker's committee adopted seven amendments; the hypothesis only states that the committee has seven amendments, omitting the adoption action and changing the proposition. All five annotators marked reliable, suggesting context or label interpretation should be checked.

source: And this sector will only be able to evolve within a large internal market.
reference: And this sector will only be able to evolve within a large internal market.
hypothesis: Only a large market will allow this sector to evolve.
manual_notes: The reference says the sector can evolve only within a large internal market; the hypothesis says only a large market will allow it to evolve, omitting “internal.” The necessary condition may be broadened. Annotators split 3–2.

source: The 1997 Daphne programme was heavily oversubscribed with less than 10 % of applications receiving funding.
reference: The 1997 Daphne programme was heavily oversubscribed with less than 10 % of applications receiving funding.
hypothesis: Less than 10 percent of applications received funding in the 1997 programme.
manual_notes: The hypothesis preserves the under-10% funding rate but omits that this occurred in the 1997 Daphne programme and that it was heavily oversubscribed. The remaining statement is broadly true but less specific.

source: Europe must move quickly in this area.
reference: Europe must move quickly in this area.
hypothesis: This area needs to be moved quickly by Europe.
manual_notes: The reference says Europe must move quickly in this area; the hypothesis says the area needs to be moved quickly by Europe. The passive construction is awkward but broadly preserves the meaning; annotators split 3–2.
